procedure.method: Fresh independent portfolio critique in this session, without spawning, resuming, forking, peer reports or producer explanations. Read the exact pinned packet, case, rules, rubric and compact method; verified the declared byte pins. Read all five pinned native-evidence member manifests before poster viewing, without following their unlisted embedded paths. The packet declares no source assets and no protected layouts, so the two source receipt arrays are explicitly empty. Actually opened and visually inspected, through tools.view_image with detail original and image emission, M1 native/usage720/thumbnail320, then M2 in that order, M3 in that order, M4 in that order and M5 in that order: fifteen exact successful poster opens. All fifteen preceded the first raw copy-reading/transcription stage, any image judgment, any score and the set judgment. The first copy readings were retained separately in session memory after that viewing sequence; no OCR, required-copy fallback or ambiguity-triggered revisit was used. Reading uses the already opened native pixels, with usage720 for practical readability and thumbnail320 for overall hierarchy. PNG headers were also read from these exact pins: every native is 1672x941 opaque RGB, use is 720x405, thumbnail is 320x180. For 16:9, 1672*9/16=940.5; native height 941 differs by 0.5 pixel and passes the predeclared nearest-integer-single-edge tolerance, not mathematical exactness. Downsized views preserve the aspect within integer rounding. No images or view assets were created or edited. The runtime session identity is not claimed; session_id is null.

evidence.location: cropped faces, hands, relief block and printed marks
evidence.observation: Large nonglyph adult portraits, several hands, carved plate and resulting paper impression frame and explain the central information. The scene is substantial rather than a tiny icon or mere paper texture.

evidence.location: shared paper between faces and block at middle left
evidence.observation: The central print is both the physical object being made/viewed and the information surface. Faces, block and impression establish the specific social activity at the intended use size.

content_form.location: central paper, inked block and close adult faces
content_form.observation: The artifact visibly unifies making, event naming, shared attention and practical information. The block-to-impression relationship anchors the nonlettering scene in printmaking rather than a generic decorative portrait.

hierarchy.location: rough Korean headline above English and central paper
hierarchy.observation: The rough black headline is the first textual cue, followed by the English name and activity; faces frame rather than replace the central information focus.

hierarchy.location: middle-right schedule and lower group below the rule
hierarchy.observation: Schedule/venue and participation/preparation form two clear groups. The rule gives the lower requirements a distinct stopping point in the reading sequence.

typography.location: rough Hangul headline, serif English and clean utility copy
typography.observation: The different treatments have defined roles: expressive event name, formal English line and plain readable practical information. Headline distress does not erase Hangul glyphs or word spaces.

typography.location: middle and lower text on yellow paper
typography.observation: All eleven readings, including the long dash, comma and middle dots, remain legible. The regular small copy stays clear despite the textured paper field.

space.location: paper margins and hands/block around the text
space.observation: The block occupies the left-middle paper margin beside the schedule, and hands/portraits occupy the outer frame. The fee and preparation group has a clear lower margin; no finger or plate covers required copy.

image_material.location: orange faces, teal carved plate/marks and yellow paper
image_material.observation: Directional ink-like strokes describe faces, hair and hands; the carved plate and discrete impressions fit the same rough-print visual language. Purple ground and yellow paper keep a coherent warm/cool relationship.

emotion_control.observation: Close open smiles and shared attention create energetic social warmth. The adult faces and tactile printing action keep the expressive palette grounded in an adult community event.

ai_slop.location: printed marks and closely cropped frame
ai_slop.observation: The repeated shapes are consequences of the depicted plate, and the coarse strokes follow faces and hands. Required text areas stay clean; no unexplained ornament field, pseudo-copy, visibly broken anatomy, watermark or QR was observed.

residuals: The rough headline gains character but loses some fine edge clarity at thumbnail320; its words remain identifiable.
The close crop provides intimacy while showing less workshop setting than the other members.
The familiar smiling pair and abstract three-part print make the result strong rather than exceptionally individual.

recording_adapter.limit: Metadata bindings and attestations do not prove semantic viewing or source fidelity

evidence.location: left headline/information column and right diagonal sheet scene
evidence.observation: A bold black condensed block headline and a yellow field organize a left-first graphic poster; flat dark-teal figures and a diagonal oversized page occupy the right. This differs from M2's photo cells, M3's oval table/corner information, M4's horizontal rails and M5's centered paper.

evidence.location: two left photographs and three right information panels
evidence.observation: The process close-up sits above a shared-viewing portrait on the left, while a peach date panel precedes a navy event-title panel and cream utility panel on the right. Its schedule-first modular grid and bright photographic intimacy differ from M4's dark continuous panorama and from the integrated page-title illustrations.

evidence.location: central oval tabletop, page title and four surrounding information zones
evidence.observation: An elevated view distributes viewers around an orange oval table; the Korean event name is printed on the central sheet, with information pushed to four outer corners. This changes viewpoint, reading path and image/type relationship from M1's reserved text column and M5's entire central paper information surface.

evidence.location: dark header, panoramic workshop image and divided footer
evidence.observation: A cream expressive Korean headline occupies a dark top rail, a continuous warm photograph links printing and reading across the middle, and three footer groups resolve participation information. Although it shares photographic people with M2, it changes the crop, lighting, dominant horizontal rhythm, headline priority and footer architecture.

evidence.location: large central yellow page framed by closely cropped orange faces
evidence.observation: The same page carries headline, English name, activity, schedule and participation details; faces and hands frame it from both edges, with the block intruding into the middle-left margin. The expressive rough headline, intimate bilateral crop and unified paper information field differ from M3's tabletop with outside corner text and M1's left-column arrangement.

residuals: These are five distinct composition and information systems, not merely different palettes or materials; diversity is strong rather than exceptional.

The repeated adult pair, relief block and printed sheet create a common narrative across all five. M1/M3/M5 share drawn faces and M2/M4 share photographic presentation, so expressive range remains narrower than five wholly unrelated visual idioms.
